chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muharibi, from Ahmad ibn Maytham, from Muhammad ibn 'Asim, from 'Abdillah ibn al-Najjar, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and ride ships?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you not know that if it drowns you, a caller will call out to you: 'Be delighted and enjoy the pleasures of Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for traveling by ship to visit Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) reveals a specific divine address ('Confidential Discourse') granted to those who undertake the journey to Karbala, emphasizing that the mode of transport is secondary to the intent of devotion. The narration highlights the Shia theological concept of *tawassul* through physical effort and risk, where even death during the pilgrimage is transformed into an immediate entry to Paradise, underscoring the high spiritual status of the Ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 10. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdān Al-Qalānisi, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain Al-Muḥāribi, from Aḥmad ibn Maytham, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Āsim, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Al-Najjār, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) asked me, “Do you go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) by ship?” I replied, “Yes.” Imam (a.s.) said, “Do you not know that if it drowns, a caller will call out to you, ‘Be delighted and enjoy the pleasures of Paradise.”
